assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational framework for valuing exhaustible natural capital, biodiversity, and sustainable economic development, with unusually broad consequences for both theory and public policy.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are central architects of the economic analysis of natural-resource depletion and its implications for welfare and growth.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has shaped environmental economics for decades and is mature enough to assess independently of immediate policy fashion.
uncertainties: The inclusive-wealth and biodiversity components encompass a broad literature, making the precise boundary of the cited contribution difficult to draw.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work made political incentives, institutions, and state capacity central objects of rigorous economic analysis, transforming political economy.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini provided core formal and empirical foundations; Besley made closely related and distinctive contributions on accountability, institutions, and public finance.
assessment.maturity: The research program is long established, influential across fields, and repeatedly applied to consequential institutional questions.
uncertainties: The wide scope of political economy complicates a compact attribution among several major contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and financial-accelerator mechanisms supplied a durable explanation for how financial frictions amplify macroeconomic fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore developed the seminal collateral framework, while Gertler made foundational linked contributions to the financial accelerator.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have been extensively incorporated into macroeconomic theory and evaluated against financial-crisis experience.
uncertainties: The candidate bundles related but not identical frameworks, and the appropriate allocation of credit beyond the proposed trio is contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection fundamentally changed the analysis of trade, productivity, market reallocation, and welfare gains from globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplied the defining heterogeneous-firm model, with Helpman and Redding contributing major extensions and applications within the same research program.
assessment.maturity: The framework is a standard part of modern trade economics and has generated a large empirical and quantitative literature.
uncertainties: The centrality of Melitz is especially clear, while the case for a joint award with the other proposed contributors requires careful delimitation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic discrete-choice methods opened empirical analysis of forward-looking decisions in settings ranging from labour and industrial organization to transportation.
assessment.attribution: Rust's methodological contribution is exceptionally identifiable and provides the core intellectual breakthrough of the candidate.
assessment.maturity: Its long use, extensive extension, and broad practical adoption establish its enduring importance.
uncertainties: The full structural dynamic-programming literature has many contributors, so the boundary between the seminal contribution and subsequent advances merits scrutiny.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification changed econometric practice by demonstrating how credible conclusions can be drawn when strong point-identifying assumptions are unjustified.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the singularly identifiable originator of the modern partial-identification program represented here.
assessment.maturity: The approach has had sustained methodological influence and is broadly relevant wherever data cannot fully identify structural objects.
uncertainties: The listed candidate combines partial identification with later moment-inequality work whose attribution is more dispersed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of misallocation connected micro-level distortions to large aggregate productivity and income differences, giving a powerful quantitative lens on development and growth.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow, and Restuccia made complementary central contributions to the influential misallocation research program.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been widely used, tested, and debated across countries and has become a central benchmark in quantitative development.
uncertainties: Inferences from measured wedges to underlying distortions remain model-dependent, and the literature continues to debate their interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression supplied a simple, general, and highly influential way to analyze how covariates affect an entire distribution rather than only its mean.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett jointly introduced the foundational method and are clearly attributable for its central innovation.
assessment.maturity: The method has proved durable across econometrics and applied economics, with a vast subsequent methodological literature.
uncertainties: The candidate's broader distributional-methods framing includes later advances with additional contributors.
